speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You are presenting with double vision, difficulty climbing stairs, and upper limb weakness; to understand the underlying cause, can you tell me when these symptoms first started and if they worsen with exertion?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detail; the pattern of worsening with exertion and improving with rest is very specific. Do you experience any drooping of your eyelids or difficulty swallowing, and have you noticed these symptoms fluctuate significantly throughout the day?

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had recent infections or fevers, and there is no family history of neurological disease. The weakness feels symmetrical in both arms and legs.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis. The combination of ocular symptoms (diplopia), symmetric limb weakness, and distinct fatigue with rest confirming the clinical picture.
